questions.question: In which state is Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the **Adilabad district** of Telangana.
 
• The sanctuary spans an area of approximately **893 square kilometers**.
 
• It was declared a wildlife sanctuary in **1965** to protect its rich biodiversity and wildlife.
 
• Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary is known for its population of **tigers, leopards, and deer**.
 
• In 2012, it was designated as a **Tiger Reserve** under Project Tiger to ensure better conservation efforts for the tiger population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Project Tiger**

 
 
• It is a tiger conservation program launched in India in **1973**.
 
• The aim is to protect tigers from extinction by ensuring a viable population in their natural habitats.
 
• Project Tiger focuses on habitat preservation, anti-poaching measures, and scientific management.
 
• India has over **50 tiger reserves** under this project, covering various regions across the country.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspot**
 
 
• A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with a significant reservoir of biodiversity that is under threat from humans.
 
• To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot, a region must contain at least **1,500 species of vascular plants** as endemics.
 
• It must have lost at least **70% of its original habitat**.
 
• The Eastern Himalayas and Western Ghats in India are examples of biodiversity hotspots.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Sanctuary**
 
 
• A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area reserved for the conservation of wild animals and their habitats.
 
• Human activities such as cultivation, grazing, and forestry are regulated to ensure minimal disturbance to wildlife.
 
• India has over **500 wildlife sanctuaries**, each focusing on preserving different species and ecosystems.
 
• Examples include Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, Jim Corbett National Park, and Kaziranga National Park.
 
 
 
• **Ecotourism**
 
 
• Ecotourism is a form of sustainable travel that supports the conservation of natural environments.
 
• It aims to minimize the negative impact on the environment and local communities.
 
• Ecotourism promotes responsible travel practices, environmental education, and cultural awareness.
 
• Popular ecotourism destinations in India include Periyar National Park, Sunderbans, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which Union Territory has the lowest proportion of poor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, **Puducherry** has the lowest proportion of poor among the Union Territories.
 
• The MPI is developed by the NITI Aayog in collaboration with Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The index measures poverty based on various factors such as health, education, and living standards.
 
• Puducherry's low poverty rate is attributed to its higher levels of education, better healthcare facilities, and improved living standards.
 
• The data reflects the effectiveness of social welfare programs and policies implemented in the Union Territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• The MPI is a comprehensive measure of poverty that considers multiple deprivations at the household level across three dimensions: health, education, and living standards.
 
• It uses 10 indicators including nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.
 
• The index provides a more nuanced understanding of poverty beyond income-based measures.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established to replace the Planning Commission.
 
• It aims to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states on a continuous basis.
 
 
 
• **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**
 
 
• OPHI is an economic research centre within the University of Oxford.
 
• It develops and implements multidimensional approaches to measuring poverty and wellbeing.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**
 
 
• UNDP is the United Nations' global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life.
 
• It works in nearly 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India specifically addresses the qualifications for the office of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 58**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 58** of the Indian Constitution lays down the qualifications required for a person to be eligible for election as the President of India.
 
• The candidate must be a citizen of India.
 
• The candidate must have completed the age of 35 years.
 
• The candidate must be qualified for election as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• The candidate should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of the said Governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 52** of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a President of India.
 
• **Article 53** states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• **Article 54** specifies the manner of election of the President.
 
• **Article 55** outlines the procedure for the election of the President.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament, as well as elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.

questions.question: Who among the following was the most important god of the Aryans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indra was the most important god of the Vedic Aryans and was considered the king of the gods.
 
• He was primarily known as the god of rain, thunder, and war, and was often invoked for victory in battles.
 
• Indra is frequently mentioned in the Rigveda, one of the oldest sacred texts of the Aryans, with over 250 hymns dedicated to him.
 
• He played a crucial role in Aryan mythology, often depicted as slaying the serpent Vritra, a symbol of drought, to release the waters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agni**

 
 
• Agni was another prominent deity of the Aryans, known as the god of fire.
 
• He acted as a mediator between the gods and humans, carrying offerings to the gods through fire.
 
• Agni played a vital role in Vedic rituals and sacrifices.
 
 
 
• **Pashupatinath**
 
 
• Pashupatinath is a form of Lord Shiva, a major deity in later Hinduism, but not prominent in early Aryan worship.
 
• The deity is revered as the lord of animals and is particularly worshipped in Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Marut**
 
 
• Maruts were storm deities, often associated with Indra in the Rigveda.
 
• They were considered the sons of Rudra and were known for their fierce nature and thunderous power.

questions.question: When was the All Bengal Students Conference held in the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The All Bengal Students Conference was held in 1928.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the conference, marking a significant moment in the Indian student movement.
 
• The conference was pivotal in galvanizing student support for the Indian independence movement.
 
• It provided a platform for young intellectuals to discuss and address national issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**

 
 
• He was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement and the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• Nehru played a key role in shaping modern India with his vision of a secular and socialist nation.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing institutions of higher learning and research in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Independence Movement**
 
 
• The movement aimed at ending British rule in India, culminating in independence in 1947.
 
• It involved a series of political and social campaigns, led by figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• Key events included the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Student Movements in India**
 
 
• Student movements have historically played a crucial role in Indian politics and social reform.
 
• They have been instrumental in advocating for educational reforms, social justice, and political change.
 
• Prominent student organizations include the All India Students Federation (AISF) and the National Students' Union of India (NSUI).
 
 
 
• **Bengal in the Independence Movement**
 
 
• Bengal was a major center for revolutionary activities against British rule.
 
• It produced several prominent leaders and revolutionaries, including Subhas Chandra Bose and Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• The region witnessed significant events such as the Partition of Bengal in 1905 and the Bengal Famine of 1943.

questions.question: The autobiography of which of the following actors is titled 'The Substance And The Shadow: An Autobiography'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dilip Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dilip Kumar**, a legendary actor in Indian cinema, is known for his significant contributions to the film industry.
 
• His autobiography, titled **'The Substance And The Shadow: An Autobiography'**, offers a detailed account of his life and illustrious career.
 
• The book was published in **2014** and has been highly acclaimed for its in-depth portrayal of his journey.
 
• Dilip Kumar, often referred to as the **'Tragedy King'**, has won numerous awards and accolades for his performances over several decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dilip Kumar's Real Name:** His birth name is Muhammad Yusuf Khan, and he adopted the screen name Dilip Kumar for his acting career.
 
• **Career Highlights:** He debuted in the film **'Jwar Bhata'** in 1944 and went on to star in classics like 'Mughal-e-Azam', 'Naya Daur', and 'Devdas'.
 
• **Honors and Awards:** Dilip Kumar received numerous awards, including **eight Filmfare Awards for Best Actor** and the **Padma Bhushan** and **Padma Vibhushan** from the Government of India.
 
• **Influence and Legacy:** He is considered one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, influencing several generations of actors with his method acting style.

questions.question: What is the name of Formula E's first ever race in India, which was hosted in collaboration with the Telangana government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The 2023 Greenko Hyderabad E-Prix**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first-ever Formula E race in India was hosted in Hyderabad in 2023.
 
• The event was officially named The 2023 Greenko Hyderabad E-Prix.
 
• It was held in collaboration with the Telangana government, highlighting the region's commitment to promoting electric vehicles and sustainable practices.
 
• The race took place on a specially designed street circuit in Hyderabad, showcasing the city's infrastructure and capability to host international sporting events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formula E**

 
 
• Formula E is a single-seater motorsport championship that uses only electric cars.
 
• It was conceived in 2011 and the inaugural championship started in Beijing in 2014.
 
• The series was created to promote electric vehicles and sustainable mobility solutions.
 
• Formula E races take place on temporary street circuits in major cities around the world.
 
 
 
• **Greenko**
 
 
• Greenko is one of India’s leading renewable energy companies.
 
• The company focuses on generating energy from renewable sources such as solar, wind, and hydro.
 
• Greenko's collaboration in hosting the E-Prix aligns with its mission to promote sustainable and clean energy solutions.
 
 
 
• **Telangana Government**
 
 
• Telangana is a state in southern India, known for its tech-savvy governance and rapid development.
 
• The state government is actively promoting the adoption of electric vehicles and sustainable practices.
 
• Hosting the Formula E race was a part of its broader strategy to position Hyderabad as a hub for innovation and sustainability.

questions.question: During which centuries did several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars travel to China on the historic 'silk route'?

options.text: First, second and third centuries AD

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First, second and third centuries AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars, such as **Faxian**, travelled to China during the first, second, and third centuries AD.
 
• These journeys were primarily taken to collect Buddhist scriptures and spread Buddhism in China.
 
• Notable figures like **Faxian** and **Kashyapa Matanga** played crucial roles in the cultural exchanges between India and China during this period.
 
• The Silk Route was a vital conduit for not only trade but also for cultural and religious exchanges.
 
• These travels significantly influenced the development of Buddhism in China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faxian**:

 
 
• Faxian was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled to India between 399 and 412 AD to collect Buddhist texts.
 
• His journey is documented in his travelogue, "A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms."
 
 
 
• **Silk Route**:
 
 
• The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade routes that connected the East and West.
 
• It was central to cultural interaction through regions of the Asian continent connecting the East and West from China to the Mediterranean Sea.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in China**:
 
 
• Buddhism was introduced to China during the Han dynasty (206 BC–220 AD).
 
• It became one of the major religions in China, influencing Chinese culture, philosophy, and art.
 
 
 
• **Kashyapa Matanga**:
 
 
• Kashyapa Matanga was an Indian Buddhist monk who is traditionally thought to have first arrived in China in the 1st century AD.
 
• He is credited with helping to establish Buddhism in China.

questions.question: Non-polar molecules possess ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **instantaneous dipole moment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Non-polar molecules have an even distribution of electrons across the molecule, resulting in no regions of partial positive or negative charge.
 
• These molecules typically consist of identical atoms or atoms with similar electronegativities, such as in diatomic molecules like N₂ or O₂.
 
• Non-polar molecules do not have a permanent dipole moment, meaning they do not have a net separation of electrical charge.
 
• Even though non-polar molecules have no permanent dipole moment, they can still possess a temporary **"instantaneous dipole moment"** due to the random fluctuations in their electron clouds, which can create a temporary positive and negative charge separation within the molecule. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• Examples of non-polar molecules include noble gases (e.g., He, Ne) and hydrocarbons like methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity:** It is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons. Non-polar bonds occur when atoms have similar electronegativities.
 
• **Polar vs. Non-polar:** Polar molecules have a significant difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms, creating partial charges and a dipole moment. Non-polar molecules do not exhibit these characteristics.
 
• **Van der Waals Forces:** Non-polar molecules primarily interact through Van der Waals forces, which are weaker than the dipole-dipole interactions found in polar molecules.
 
• **Solubility:** Non-polar molecules are generally soluble in non-polar solvents (like oils and fats) but insoluble in polar solvents (like water).
 
• **Instantaneous Dipole:** Although non-polar molecules do not have a permanent dipole moment, they can have instantaneous dipoles due to temporary imbalances in electron distribution, leading to weak London dispersion forces.

questions.question: The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is an example of the _______ industry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**public sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is a **public sector undertaking (PSU)** in India.
 
• SAIL is one of the largest steel-making companies in India and one of the **Maharatnas of India's Central Public Sector Enterprises**.
 
• It was established in 1973 and operates under the **Ministry of Steel, Government of India**.
 
• SAIL owns and operates **five integrated steel plants** at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, and Burnpur (Asansol), and three special steel plants at Salem, Durgapur, and Bhadravati.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**

 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations or state-owned enterprises created by the government to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• These entities are either wholly or partially owned by the government and are typically involved in industries considered crucial for the country's economy.
 
 
 
• **Maharatna Status**
 
 
• This status is granted to select CPSEs to empower them to expand operations and emerge as global giants.
 
• Companies with Maharatna status have greater autonomy compared to other PSUs in terms of investment decisions, mergers, and acquisitions.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Steel**
 
 
• This is the apex body responsible for formulating policies and strategies for the growth of the steel industry in India.
 
• The ministry ensures coordination among various stakeholders, including public and private sector steel companies.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Steel Plants**
 
 
• These are large-scale industrial setups that carry out all processes from raw material processing to finished steel production.
 
• They include various stages such as coke production, sintering, iron making, steel making, and rolling.

questions.question: Who among the following led the Parliamentary delegation to participate in the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in September 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harivansh Narayan Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harivansh Narayan Singh, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, led the Indian Parliamentary delegation to the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
 
• The forum took place in September 2023, focusing on strengthening parliamentary cooperation among BRICS nations.
 
• Harivansh Narayan Singh's participation underscores India's active role in BRICS and its commitment to multilateralism.
 
• The BRICS Parliamentary Forum is a platform for parliamentarians from Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa to discuss and promote common interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS**

 
 
• BRICS stands for Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, representing major emerging economies.
 
• The group was formed in 2009 with the aim of promoting peace, security, and development in the region.
 
• BRICS nations account for about 42% of the world's population and 23% of the global GDP.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Forums**
 
 
• Parliamentary forums like the BRICS Parliamentary Forum facilitate dialogue and cooperation on legislative matters.
 
• They provide a platform for parliamentarians to share best practices and collaborate on global issues.
 
 
 
• **Harivansh Narayan Singh**
 
 
• He is a seasoned politician and journalist, serving as the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha since 2018.
 
• He has played a significant role in various parliamentary committees and discussions.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Cooperation**
 
 
• BRICS nations collaborate on various fronts including economic, political, and cultural exchanges.
 
• They work together to address global challenges like climate change, terrorism, and economic inequality.

questions.question: As per Article 51A of the Constitution of India, Fundamental Duty (h) is to develop the ______________, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**scientific temper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 51A(h)** of the Constitution of India lists the fundamental duty to develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• The concept of **scientific temper** was promoted by the first Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• Scientific temper refers to an **attitude of logical and rational thinking**.
 
• This duty aims to encourage **critical thinking and scientific reasoning** among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• These duties are listed in **Part IV-A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties, but an eleventh duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Temper**
 
 
• Scientific temper is a way of life that involves the application of logic and the avoidance of superstition and irrational beliefs.
 
• It is essential for the progress and development of society.
 
• Promoting scientific temper is also crucial for fostering innovation and technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Humanism**
 
 
• Humanism is a rational philosophy informed by science, inspired by art, and motivated by compassion.
 
• It affirms the dignity and worth of all people and promotes human welfare and happiness.
 
 
 
• **Spirit of Inquiry**
 
 
• The spirit of inquiry involves curiosity, questioning, and the search for truth and knowledge.
 
• It encourages people to challenge established norms and contribute to societal reforms.

questions.question: Which classical dance form is performed by the renowned artists; Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnaal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated from the **northern regions of India** and has a rich tradition of storytelling through dance.
 
• Famous exponents of Kathak include **Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnaal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia, and Uma Sharma**.
 
• Kathak is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form is closely associated with the **Hindu epics** and the **Bhakti movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gharanas**

 
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools): **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras**.
 
• Each gharana has its own unique style and repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Music**
 
 
• Male dancers typically wear **dhoti-kurta**, while female dancers wear **lehenga-choli** or **saree**.
 
• The music is mainly based on **Hindustani classical music**.
 
 
 
• **Instruments**
 
 
• The main instruments used in Kathak performances include **tabla**, **harmonium**, and **sitar**.
 
• The dancers also wear **ghungroos** (ankle bells) to emphasize their footwork.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Kathak evolved from the **ancient storytellers** known as Kathakars.
 
• It was influenced by both **Hindu and Muslim cultures** during the Mughal era.

questions.question: Select the synthetic indicator from among the given options.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methyl orange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Methyl orange** is a synthetic indicator used primarily in titrations due to its clear and distinct color change.
 
• It is used to determine the pH of a solution, changing color at a pH of approximately 3.1 to 4.4.
 
• In acidic solutions, methyl orange turns red, whereas in basic solutions, it turns yellow.
 
• This indicator is particularly useful for titrations involving weak bases and strong acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Litmus Solution**

 
 
• Litmus is a natural indicator derived from lichens.
 
• It is commonly used to test whether a solution is acidic or basic.
 
• Acidic solutions turn blue litmus paper red, while basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric**
 
 
• Turmeric is a natural indicator that turns red in basic conditions.
 
• It remains yellow in acidic and neutral solutions.
 
• It is commonly used in household experiments to test for the presence of bases.
 
 
 
• **Cabbage Juice**
 
 
• Red cabbage juice is a natural pH indicator.
 
• It changes color over a wide pH range, from red in acidic conditions to green/yellow in neutral conditions, and blue/purple in basic conditions.
 
• It is often used in educational settings for pH experiments.
 
 
 
• **Indicators**
 
 
• An indicator is a substance that changes color to indicate the presence of an acid or base.
 
• They are widely used in titrations to determine the endpoint of a chemical reaction.
 
• Indicators can be synthetic (like methyl orange) or natural (like litmus, turmeric, and cabbage juice).

questions.question: The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in which of the following present states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in the present state of Maharashtra.
 
• The Ramoshi community, primarily residing in Maharashtra, revolted against the British East India Company.
 
• The uprising was led by Chittur Singh, a notable leader of the Ramoshi tribe.
 
• The Ramoshis were dissatisfied with British policies that impacted their traditional way of life and economic conditions.
 
• This uprising was one of the early revolts against British colonial rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramoshi Community**

 
 
• The Ramoshis are a tribal community found mainly in Maharashtra and parts of Karnataka.
 
• Traditionally, they were known for their skills in hunting and gathering, and later some were employed as watchmen and guards.
 
• Their traditional leadership and warrior skills were significant during the Maratha Empire.
 
 
 
• **British Policies and Impact**
 
 
• The British East India Company implemented policies that disrupted the traditional livelihoods of many tribal communities.
 
• Land revenue policies and forest laws restricted the Ramoshis' access to their traditional lands and resources.
 
• These policies led to widespread discontent and resistance among various tribal groups in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Uprisings**
 
 
• The Santal Rebellion (1855-56) in present-day Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• The Bhil Uprising (1818-1831) in western India.
 
• The Munda Rebellion (1899-1900) led by Birsa Munda in present-day Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• These uprisings were among the early signs of resistance against colonial rule in India.
 
• They reflect the widespread discontentment among various communities due to the exploitative policies of the British.
 
• Such uprisings set the stage for a broader national movement for independence in the later years.

questions.question: In October 2023, Maharashtra government planned which of the following schemes to overhaul its medical system after the death of 38 patients in Nanded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vision 2035**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maharashtra government introduced the **Vision 2035** plan to modernize and revamp its healthcare system.
 
• This initiative comes in response to the tragic deaths of 38 patients in a government hospital in Nanded in October 2023.
 
• **Vision 2035** aims to upgrade medical facilities, infrastructure, and healthcare services across the state.
 
• The plan includes the integration of advanced medical technologies and training programs for healthcare professionals.
 
• The Maharashtra government is committed to ensuring better healthcare delivery and patient safety through this comprehensive scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**

 
 
• It is a national health insurance scheme spearheaded by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• It is considered to be the world's largest government-financed health assurance initiative.
 
• It aims to provide free access to health insurance coverage for India's low-income earners.
 
• AB-PMJAY provides a cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• This scheme is fully financed by the Indian government, serving as a significant step towards universal healthcare in India.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**
 
 
• It is a government-backed accident insurance scheme launched on May 9, 2015, by PM Narendra Modi.
 
• PMSBY aims to provide affordable insurance for the poor and underprivileged.
 
• Available to individuals aged 18 to 70 years with a bank account.
 
• For an annual premium of Rs.12, beneficiaries receive coverage of Rs.2 lakh for accidental death and full disability, and Rs.1 lakh for partial disability.
 
• This scheme plays a pivotal role in protecting vulnerable individuals from unforeseen risks.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)**
 
 
• Launched on May 9, 2015, by PM Narendra Modi.
 
• A government-backed life insurance scheme aimed at increasing life insurance coverage.
 
• Available to individuals aged 18 to 50 years with a bank account.
 
• Offers a life cover of Rs.2 lakhs for a one-year period, renewable annually.
 
• The annual premium is Rs.436, automatically debited from the subscriber's account.
 
• This scheme provides affordable life insurance to Indian citizens.

questions.question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A and column-B?

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 **Column-A (Food component)**
 **Column-B (Enzyme involved in digestion)**
 
 

 i. Protein
 a. Amylase
 
 

 ii. Carbohydrates
 b. Lipase
 
 

 iii. Fats
 c. Trypsin
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1: i-c, ii-a, iii-b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Proteins** are broken down by the enzyme **Trypsin**, which is produced in the pancreas and acts in the small intestine.
 
• **Carbohydrates** are digested by **Amylase**, an enzyme found in saliva and pancreatic juice.
 
• **Fats** are digested by the enzyme **Lipase**, which is also produced in the pancreas and acts in the small intestine.
 
• Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up the chemical reactions involved in the digestion of food.
 
• The correct matching of Column-A and Column-B is: i) Protein - Trypsin, ii) Carbohydrates - Amylase, iii) Fats - Lipase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proteins:** Complex molecules that are broken down into amino acids, which are essential for various body functions.
 
• **Carbohydrates:** Organic compounds that serve as a major energy source for the body, broken down into simple sugars like glucose.
 
• **Fats:** Lipid molecules that are broken down into fatty acids and glycerol, providing a concentrated energy source.
 
• **Amylase:** An enzyme that helps in the breakdown of starches into sugars, found in saliva and pancreatic juice.
 
• **Trypsin:** A protease enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides, produced by the pancreas.
 
• **Lipase:** An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of fats into fatty acids and glycerol, essential for fat digestion and absorption.

questions.question: A process like river bifurcation can create valuable landforms for the environment, providing growth of vegetation. An example of such landform is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**river deltas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• River deltas are formed at the mouth of a river where it meets a standing body of water like an ocean, sea, or lake, leading to sediment deposition.
 
• They are highly fertile areas due to the accumulation of nutrient-rich sediments, supporting diverse vegetation and agriculture.
 
• The process of bifurcation, where a river splits into multiple channels, contributes to the creation and expansion of delta regions.
 
• Famous examples of river deltas include the Nile Delta in Egypt, the Mississippi Delta in the USA, and the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta in India and Bangladesh.
 
• Deltas play a crucial role in sustaining ecosystems, supporting wildlife habitats, and providing protection against storm surges and coastal erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sedimentation Process**

 
 
• Rivers carry sediments which are deposited when the river loses its carrying capacity upon entering a slower-moving or standing body of water.
 
• This process gradually builds up layers of sediment, forming the delta.
 
 
 
• **Bifurcation**
 
 
• Bifurcation refers to a river splitting into two or more channels, contributing to the formation of distributaries in delta regions.
 
• This division helps in the even distribution of sediments across the delta area.
 
 
 
• **Types of Deltas**
 
 
• There are several types of deltas based on their shape and formation process, including arcuate, bird's foot, and cuspate deltas.
 
• For example, the Nile Delta is an arcuate delta, while the Mississippi Delta is a bird's foot delta.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**
 
 
• Deltas are critical for biodiversity, providing habitats for various species of fish, birds, and other wildlife.
 
• They also act as natural buffers, absorbing floodwaters and reducing the impact of storm surges.
 
 
 
• **Human Impact**
 
 
• Human activities such as dam construction and river channelization can significantly affect sediment flow and delta formation.
 
• Efforts are being made to manage and restore delta regions to maintain their ecological and economic benefits.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by who among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• The construction of the Taj Mahal was completed in 1653, employing thousands of artisans and craftsmen.
 
• The Taj Mahal is located on the southern bank of the Yamuna River in the city of Agra, India.
 
• This architectural marvel is renowned for its stunning white marble dome and intricate inlay work with precious stones.
 
• The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is often regarded as the pinnacle of Mughal architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Architecture:**

 
 
• Mughal architecture is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets at the corners, massive halls, and large vaulted gateways.
 
• It combines elements from Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• Examples include the Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, and the Jama Masjid in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal Emperor, reigning from 1628 to 1658.
 
• He is also known for commissioning other significant buildings such as the Red Fort in Delhi and the Jama Masjid.
 
• His reign is often considered the golden age of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• World Heritage Sites are landmarks or areas with legal protection by an international convention administered by UNESCO.
 
• They are recognized for having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River:**
 
 
• The Yamuna River is one of the major rivers of India and the longest tributary of the Ganges.
 
• It flows through several states including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE for the Harappan town planning?

1. Most of the towns have citadel in harappan civilization.

2. Every town had a temple in Harappan civilization.

3. Every building was made of sand stone in Harappan civilization.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its advanced town planning, including features like grid layouts and well-organized drainage systems.
 
• Most Harappan towns had a citadel, which served as a fortified area housing important buildings and possibly administrative centers.
 
• There is no evidence that every town had a temple; instead, the civilization is known for its secular architecture.
 
• Harappan buildings were primarily constructed using baked bricks, not sandstone.
 
• The cities featured well-planned streets, granaries, and public baths, reflecting advanced urban planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citadel:** A raised area in Harappan cities that housed important buildings and possibly served as a center for administration and storage.
 
• **Drainage System:** Harappan cities had sophisticated drainage systems with covered drains running alongside the streets, indicating advanced engineering skills.
 
• **Granaries:** Large storage structures found in some Harappan cities, suggesting the importance of agriculture and surplus storage in their economy.
 
• **Public Baths:** Structures like the Great Bath in Mohenjo-Daro, indicating the emphasis on cleanliness and possibly ritual bathing in Harappan culture.
 
• **Urban Planning:** The layout of Harappan cities with grid-pattern streets, standardized brick sizes, and consistent architectural planning across various settlements.

questions.question: __________ was the pioneer who modified the Hawaiian slide guitar to play classical ragas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brij Bhushan Kabra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brij Bhushan Kabra** was a pioneer in modifying the Hawaiian slide guitar to play classical ragas.
 
• He was born in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, and is renowned for his innovative approach to Indian classical music.
 
• Kabra's contribution significantly enriched the Indian classical music repertoire with the inclusion of guitar.
 
• His style brought a new dimension to Indian classical music, blending the sounds of the guitar with traditional ragas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hawaiian Slide Guitar**

 
 
• Originally used in Hawaiian music, it involves sliding a metal bar along the strings to create a smooth, gliding sound.
 
• This technique allows for a continuous range of pitches, akin to the human voice.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Ragas**
 
 
• Ragas are melodic frameworks for improvisation in Indian classical music.
 
• Each raga is associated with a specific time of day or season, and evokes particular emotions.
 
 
 
• **Fusion Music**
 
 
• Fusion music combines elements from different musical traditions, creating new and innovative sounds.
 
• Kabra's work represents a fusion of Western and Indian musical techniques.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Modern Indian Music**
 
 
• Brij Bhushan Kabra's integration of the guitar into Indian classical music paved the way for future musicians to experiment with new instruments and sounds.
 
• His legacy continues to inspire contemporary musicians to explore and innovate within the realm of Indian classical music.

questions.question: Which edition of the Intercontinental Cup event was played in India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2023 edition of the Intercontinental Cup was the **3rd edition** of the tournament.
 
• The Intercontinental Cup is a football tournament organized by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).
 
• The previous editions of the tournament were held in 2018 and 2019.
 
• The event provides international exposure to the Indian national football team by allowing them to compete against teams from different continents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**

 
 
• The AIFF is the governing body for football in India and is responsible for the promotion and development of the sport in the country.
 
• It was founded in 1937 and is affiliated with FIFA, the international governing body for football.
 
• The AIFF organizes various domestic football leagues and tournaments, including the Indian Super League (ISL) and the I-League.
 
 
 
• **Intercontinental Cup**
 
 
• The Intercontinental Cup is an invitational tournament that features teams from different continents.
 
• The primary aim of the tournament is to provide competitive international matches for the Indian national team.
 
• The first edition was held in 2018, and the tournament has since become a regular feature in the Indian football calendar.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Football Team**
 
 
• The team is governed by the AIFF and represents India in international football competitions.
 
• The team has seen significant improvements in recent years and has been actively participating in various international tournaments.
 
• Sunil Chhetri, the team captain, is one of the most prominent and successful players in Indian football history.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Intercontinental Cup**
 
 
• The tournament helps in improving the FIFA rankings of the Indian national team by providing them with competitive matches.
 
• It also helps in popularizing football in India, encouraging more young players to take up the sport.
 
• The exposure gained by playing against international teams helps in the overall development of the players and the team.

questions.question: In the context of microfinance, what does ‘S’ stand for in SHG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Self**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** are informal associations of people who choose to come together to find ways to improve their living conditions.
 
• They are usually composed of 10-20 members, often women, from similar socio-economic backgrounds.
 
• The primary objective of SHGs is to enhance the socio-economic conditions of their members through collective efforts and mutual support.
 
• SHGs play a crucial role in financial inclusion by enabling members to pool their savings, access credit, and engage in income-generating activities.
 
• SHGs are a key component of microfinance initiatives, providing a platform for the delivery of financial services to the underserved and marginalized sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance**

 
 
• Microfinance refers to the provision of financial services to low-income individuals or groups who typically lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• It includes a range of services such as microcredit, savings, insurance, and remittances.
 
• Microfinance aims to promote financial inclusion and empower economically disadvantaged people.
 
• It has been recognized as a powerful tool for poverty alleviation and socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion involves ensuring that individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services.
 
• These services should meet their needs and be delivered responsibly and sustainably.
 
• Financial inclusion is essential for reducing poverty, fostering economic growth, and promoting social equity.
 
 
 
• **Women Empowerment through SHGs**
 
 
• SHGs have been instrumental in empowering women by enhancing their financial independence and decision-making power.
 
• Participation in SHGs helps women develop skills, confidence, and a sense of solidarity.
 
• Empowered women contribute to the well-being of their families and communities, leading to broader social and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Government Support for SHGs**
 
 
• The Indian government, through various schemes and programs, supports the formation and strengthening of SHGs.
 
• Initiatives like the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) aim to promote SHGs and enhance their capacity.
 
• Government support includes financial assistance, training, and capacity-building activities for SHG members.

questions.question: In which state is 'Bhogali Bihu' festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhogali Bihu** is one of the most important festivals celebrated in the state of **Assam**.
 
• Also known as **Magh Bihu**, it marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of **Magh** (January-February).
 
• The festival is characterized by **community feasts**, bonfires, and the preparation of traditional Assamese delicacies.
 
• It is a time for farmers to relax and enjoy the fruits of their labor with family and friends.
 
• Various traditional games like **tekeli bhonga** (pot-breaking) and **buffalo fighting** are organized during the celebrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu Festival**

 
 
• There are three main types of Bihu celebrated in Assam: **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Kati Bihu** (Kongali Bihu), and **Magh Bihu** (Bhogali Bihu).
 
• Bohag Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• Kati Bihu is observed in the month of Kati (October) and is associated with the relocation of crops and the lighting of lamps.
 
• Magh Bihu, as mentioned, celebrates the end of the harvest season.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Foods**
 
 
• During Bhogali Bihu, people prepare various traditional dishes such as **pitha** (rice cakes), **laru** (coconut and sesame sweets), and **doi** (curd).
 
• Community feasts called **bhog** are organized where neighbors and relatives come together to share food.
 
 
 
• **Meji and Bhela Ghar**
 
 
• **Meji** is a bonfire made of wood and bamboo, symbolizing the end of the harvesting period.
 
• **Bhela Ghar** are temporary huts made from bamboo, leaves, and thatch, where people gather to eat and celebrate.
 
• These structures are usually burnt at the end of the festival as part of the ritual.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance**
 
 
• The festival fosters a sense of community and reinforces cultural bonds among the Assamese people.
 
• It also reflects the agrarian lifestyle of Assam, highlighting the importance of agriculture in the region.
